name: Neomycin/polymyxin B/dexamethasone (eye)
className: Eye corticosteroid with antibiotics (ophthalmological, ATC S01CA01)
searchTerms: dexamethasone neomycin polymyxin B eye drops
neomycin sulfate polymyxin B sulfate dexamethasone

formulations.label: Eye drops, suspension
formulations.strengths: Dexamethasone 1 mg / polymyxin B sulfate 6,000 IU / neomycin sulfate 3,500 IU per mL
formulations.note: Contains benzalkonium chloride 0.04 mg/mL (can be absorbed by and discolour soft contact lenses). Shake well before use.

src.q: 1 ml suspension contains 1 mg dexamethasone, 6000 IU polymyxin B sulphate, 3500 IU neomycin sulphate (as base).
1 ml suspension contains 0.04 mg benzalkonium chloride.

formulations.label: Eye ointment
formulations.strengths: Dexamethasone 1 mg / polymyxin B sulfate 6,000 IU / neomycin sulfate 3,500 IU per g
formulations.note: Contains methyl and propyl parahydroxybenzoate (possible delayed allergic reactions) and lanolin (possible contact dermatitis).

src.q: 1 gram ointment contains 1 mg dexamethasone, 6000 IU polymyxin B sulphate, and 3500 IU neomycin sulphate (as base).
This product contains methylparahydroxybenzoate and propylparahydroxybenzoate which may cause allergic reactions (possibly delayed).

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Short-term treatment of steroid-responsive eye conditions when preventive antibiotic cover is also needed, after fungal and viral disease have been excluded.

src.q: indicated for the short-term treatment of steroid responsive conditions of the eye when prophylactic antibiotic treatment is also required, after excluding the presence of fungal and viral disease

items.t: Prescription-only medicine in the UK. Short-term use only.

src.q: Prescription only medicine
indicated for the short-term treatment of steroid responsive conditions of the eye

items.t: Eye drops: 1 to 2 drops into each affected eye up to six times daily, or more often if needed.

src.q: Apply one or two drops to each affected eye up to six times daily or, more frequently if required.

items.t: Eye ointment: a small amount into the conjunctival sac(s) up to 3 to 4 times daily, or at bedtime alongside the drops.

src.q: Apply a small amount into the conjunctival sac(s) up to three to four times daily or, may be used adjunctively with drops at bedtime.

items.t: Same dose as adults. Children may have a greater and earlier risk of steroid-induced raised eye pressure; check intraocular pressure with prolonged use. Children are among those predisposed to Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression with intensive or long-term use.

src.q: Children and Adults (including the Elderly)
the risk of corticosteroid-induced ocular hypertension may be greater in children and may occur earlier than in adults
may occur after intensive or long-term continuous therapy in predisposed patients, including children

items.t: Hypersensitivity to neomycin, polymyxin B, dexamethasone or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients.

items.t: Herpes simplex keratitis; vaccinia, varicella and other viral infections of the cornea or conjunctiva.

src.q: Herpes simplex keratitis. Vaccinia, varicella, and other viral infection of cornea or conjunctiva.

items.t: Fungal disease of the eye; untreated parasitic eye infection; mycobacterial eye infection.

src.q: Fungal diseases of ocular structures or untreated parasitic eye infections. Mycobacterial ocular infections.

items.t: Prolonged eye steroid use can cause raised intraocular pressure or glaucoma (optic nerve damage, loss of vision or visual field) and posterior subcapsular cataract. Check intraocular pressure routinely and often with prolonged use. Risk is higher in predisposed patients (e.g. diabetes).

src.q: Prolonged use of ophthalmic corticosteroids may result in ocular hypertension and/or glaucoma, with damage to the optic nerve, reduced visual acuity and visual field defects, and posterior subcapsular cataract formation.
In patients receiving prolonged ophthalmic corticosteroid therapy, intraocular pressure should be checked routinely and frequently.
The risk of corticosteroid-induced raised intraocular pressure and/or cataract formation is increased in predisposed patients (e.g. diabetes).

items.t: Steroids may lower resistance to infection and mask signs of infection. Suspect fungal infection if a corneal ulcer persists; stop the steroid if fungal infection occurs. Frequent slit-lamp examination is essential to avoid worsening herpetic corneal disease.

src.q: Corticosteroids may reduce resistance to and aid in the establishment of nonsusceptible bacterial, fungal, parasitic or viral infections and mask the clinical signs of infection
corticosteroid therapy should be discontinued if fungal infection occurs
To avoid the risk of enhancement of herpetic corneal disease, frequent slit lamp examination is essential.

items.t: Diseases that thin the cornea or sclera: perforation has occurred with topical steroids. Topical eye steroids may slow corneal healing.

src.q: In those diseases causing thinning of the cornea or sclera, perforations have been known to occur with the use of topical corticosteroids.
Topical ophthalmic corticosteroids may slow corneal wound healing.

items.t: Neomycin sensitivity can occur, with possible cross-sensitivity to other aminoglycosides; reactions range from local to anaphylaxis. Stop if serious or hypersensitivity reactions occur.

src.q: Sensitivity to topically applied aminoglycosides may occur in some patients. Cross-sensitivity to other aminoglycosides may also occur.
If signs of serious reactions or hypersensitivity occur, discontinue the use of this product.

items.t: Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression can occur after intensive or long-term use in predisposed patients, including children and patients on CYP3A4 inhibitors; withdraw gradually in these cases.

src.q: Cushing's syndrome and/or adrenal suppression associated with systemic absorption of ocular dexamethasone may occur after intensive or long-term continuous therapy in predisposed patients
In these cases, treatment should be progressively discontinued.

items.t: Personal or family history of diabetes: use with caution (possible reduced glucose tolerance).

src.q: caution is recommended when administering MAXITROL to patients with a personal or family history of diabetes

items.t: Blurred vision or other visual disturbance: consider referral to an ophthalmologist (cataract, glaucoma, central serous chorioretinopathy).

src.q: the patient should be considered for referral to an ophthalmologist for evaluation of possible causes which may include cataract, glaucoma or rare diseases such as central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR)

items.t: Contact lenses are discouraged during treatment of an eye infection. Drops contain benzalkonium chloride: if lenses are allowed, remove them before use and wait 15 minutes. Use with caution in dry eye or a compromised cornea.

src.q: patients should be advised not to wear contact lenses during treatment
must be instructed to remove contact lenses prior to application of MAXITROL eye drops, suspension and wait 15 minutes after instillation of the dose before reinsertion
Should be used with caution in dry eye patients and in patients where the cornea may be compromised.

items.t: Systemic neomycin and polymyxin B can be nephrotoxic, neurotoxic and ototoxic (not reported after eye use); caution with systemic aminoglycoside or polymyxin B therapy.

src.q: Although these effects have not been reported following topical ocular use of this product, caution is advised when used concomitantly with systemic aminoglycoside or polymyxin B therapy.

items.t: CYP3A4 inhibitors (including ritonavir and cobicistat) may reduce dexamethasone clearance, causing adrenal suppression or Cushing's syndrome. Avoid unless the benefit outweighs the risk; if used, monitor for systemic steroid effects.

src.q: CYP3A4 inhibitors (including ritonavir and cobicistat): may decrease dexamethasone clearance resulting in increased effects and adrenal suppression/Cushing's syndrome.

The combination should be avoided unless the benefit outweighs the increased risk of systemic corticosteroid side-effects, in which case patients should be monitored for systemic corticosteroid effects.

items.t: Other drugs with neurotoxic, ototoxic or nephrotoxic effects (systemic, oral or topical), given at the same time or one after another: additive toxicity with neomycin; avoid whenever possible.

src.q: Concomitant and/or sequential use of an aminoglycoside (neomycin) and other systemic, oral, or topical drugs that have neurotoxic, ototoxic, or nephrotoxic effects may result in additive toxicity and should be avoided, whenever possible.

items.t: Antidiabetic medicines: a higher dose may be needed because the steroid may reduce their glucose-lowering effect.

src.q: The possibility of a higher need for hypoglycaemic medicinal products must be taken into consideration when administering MAXITROL to diabetic patients

items.t: Topical (eye) NSAIDs with topical steroids may increase corneal healing problems.

src.q: Concomitant use of topical steroids and topical NSAIDs may increase the potential for corneal healing problems.

items.t: Other eye medicines: give at least 5 minutes apart; use eye ointments last.

src.q: If more than one ophthalmic medicinal product is being used, the medicines must be administered at least 5 minutes apart. Eye ointments should be administered last.

items.t: Not studied in renal impairment; no dose adjustment needed because systemic absorption is low.

src.q: However, due to low systemic absorption of the active substances after topical administration of this product, dose adjustment is not necessary.

items.t: Not studied in hepatic impairment; no dose adjustment needed because systemic absorption is low.

src.q: However, due to low systemic absorption of the active substances after topical administration of this product, dose adjustment is not necessary.

items.t: SmPC: not recommended in pregnancy. Prolonged or repeated corticosteroid use has been linked to intrauterine growth restriction; observe newborns of mothers given substantial steroid doses for hypoadrenalism. Neomycin at this low eye dose is not expected to cause fetal ototoxicity or nephrotoxicity.

src.q: MAXITROL eye drops, suspension is not recommended during pregnancy.
Prolonged or repeated corticoid use during pregnancy has been associated with an increased risk of intra-uterine growth retardation.
At the low dose administered via this topical product, neomycin is not expected to cause ototoxicity or nephrotoxicity from in utero exposure.

items.t: BUMPS: most eye drops can be used in pregnancy because very little reaches the baby; aminoglycoside eye or ear drops do not enter the bloodstream in amounts that could harm the baby.

src.q: Most types of eye drops can be used during pregnancy.
when used in the form of eye or ear drops, do not enter the bloodstream in amounts that could harm the baby

items.t: SmPC: unknown whether excreted in milk; a risk to the infant cannot be excluded. Decide whether to stop breastfeeding or stop treatment, weighing the benefits.

src.q: Because systemic corticosteroids and aminoglycosides may be distributed into milk, a risk to the suckling child cannot be excluded.
A decision must be made whether to discontinue/abstain from breast-feeding or to discontinue therapy

items.t: SPS: dexamethasone for eye use can be used during breastfeeding with no monitoring needed; combination products containing antibiotics add no extra risk.

src.q: Dexamethasone for ophthalmic use or use in the ear can be used during breastfeeding.
There are no additional risks when combination topical preparations containing antibiotics are used.

items.t: No data on effects on male or female fertility.

src.q: There are no available data on the use of this medicine affecting male or female fertility.

items.t: No common or very common effects listed. Most frequent in trials (0.7% to 0.9%): eye discomfort, keratitis, eye irritation. Uncommon: raised intraocular pressure, eye itching.

src.q: the most common adverse reactions were ocular discomfort, keratitis, and eye irritation, occurring in 0.7% to 0.9% of patients
Uncommon: keratitis, intraocular pressure increased, eye pruritus, ocular discomfort, , eye irritation

items.t: Raised intraocular pressure with optic nerve damage, posterior subcapsular cataract, corneal thinning or perforation (especially after long treatment). Check intraocular pressure with prolonged use.

src.q: in diseases causing thinning of the cornea or sclera there is a higher risk for perforation especially after long treatments
Topical ophthalmic steroid use may result in increased intraocular pressure with damage to the optic nerve, reduced visual acuity and visual field defects.

items.t: Hypersensitivity (local to anaphylaxis), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression (frequency not known). Stop if serious reactions or hypersensitivity occur.

src.q: Not known: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
Not known: Cushing's syndrome, adrenal suppression
If signs of serious reactions or hypersensitivity occur, discontinue the use of this product.

items.t: Prolonged use: check intraocular pressure routinely and often (especially in children).

src.q: In patients receiving prolonged ophthalmic corticosteroid therapy, intraocular pressure should be checked routinely and frequently.
This is especially important in paediatric patients

items.t: Frequent slit-lamp examination to avoid worsening herpetic corneal disease.

src.q: To avoid the risk of enhancement of herpetic corneal disease, frequent slit lamp examination is essential.

items.t: With CYP3A4 inhibitors: monitor for systemic corticosteroid effects.

src.q: in which case patients should be monitored for systemic corticosteroid effects

items.t: Stop the steroid if fungal infection occurs; stop the product if serious or hypersensitivity reactions occur.

src.q: corticosteroid therapy should be discontinued if fungal infection occurs
If signs of serious reactions or hypersensitivity occur, discontinue the use of this product.

items.t: Drops: shake the bottle well. Do not let the dropper tip touch the eyelids or any surface.

src.q: Shake the bottle well before use.
caution should be exercised to ensure that the dropper tip does not touch the eyelids, the surroundings of the eye, or any other surface

items.t: Press on the inner corner of the eye (nasolacrimal occlusion) or close the eyelid gently after use to reduce systemic absorption.

src.q: Nasolacrimal occlusion or gently closing the eyelid after administration is recommended.

items.t: Ointment: do not touch the tube tip to any surface.

src.q: Do not touch the top of the tube to any surface as this may contaminate the contents.

items.t: Vision may blur for a short time after use; wait until it clears before driving or using machines.

src.q: If transient blurred vision occurs upon instillation, the patient must wait until the vision clears before driving or using machinery.

items.t: See a doctor if eye pain, redness, swelling or irritation gets worse or does not settle.

src.q: Patients using ophthalmic preparations containing neomycin sulphate should be advised to consult a physician if ocular pain, redness, swelling, or irritation worsens or persists.

items.t: Do not wear contact lenses during treatment.
